Builders exterior cleaning for handover in Melbourne

The exterior half of a handover, on your date

Render splatter, mortar, adhesive, silicone and site dust off the glazing, the driveway, the paths and the facade. Booked against a handover date rather than a rough week, and scoped to the outside so there is no overlap with your internal cleaner.

  • Booked to a handover date
  • Exterior scope only, no overlap
  • Multiple lots across one estate
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services
  3. Builders and handover cleaning

What this is

An exterior builders clean is the last trade on site before handover. Everything the build left on the outside comes off: render and paint splatter, mortar smears, tile adhesive, silicone, stickers, protective film residue, concrete slurry and the fine site dust that is on every surface.

It is deliberately only the outside. We are not an internal builders clean and we do not quote as one. Most builders already have an internal cleaner, and the two jobs want different gear, different chemistry and usually different days. Keeping the scopes separate means nothing is double paid for and nothing falls between the two of us, which is the usual failure on a handover.

Scope boundary

Ours, and the internal cleaner's

Worth agreeing before the job rather than on the morning of handover.

We do the outside

Everything on this list is in a standard exterior clean.

  • All external glazing, both faces where accessible, plus frames, tracks and sills
  • Render, paint and mortar splatter off brick, render and cladding
  • Driveway, crossover, paths and any concrete pour, including slurry and footprints
  • Alfresco, porch, patio and decking surfaces
  • Garage door, entry door, letterbox and meter box
  • Fascia, eaves, gutters externally and visible downpipes
  • Site dust rinsed off the whole facade as a final pass

The internal cleaner does the inside

We do not quote for any of this, which keeps the two scopes clean.

  • Internal floors, walls, ceilings and joinery
  • Inside faces of windows where internal access is restricted to their scope
  • Kitchens, bathrooms and appliance detailing
  • Dust from internal cavities, ducts and fixtures
  • Carpet and floor protection removal
  • Final internal detail before PCI
  • Rubbish removal and skip management

Why the glazing cannot wait until after handover

Construction deposit on glass is not dust. Render run off, concrete slurry, mortar splash and the fines from cutting all carry alkaline salts. Left on glass through a few hot days and a dew cycle, they do not sit on the surface, they etch into it.

Once that has happened the glass is permanently marked and the only fix is replacement, which at handover is a warranty claim, a delay and an argument about who pays. It is the single most common exterior defect we see raised at a pre-settlement inspection.

Cleaned before the deposit has had time to bond, the same glass comes up perfectly. That is why builders window cleaning is treated as its own task with its own timing rather than being folded into a general tidy at the end.

Protective film is not protection

Film left on frames and glass through a Melbourne summer bakes on and the adhesive transfers. Removing it then takes solvent and time, and on powder coated frames it can take the finish with it. Film should come off well before handover, not at it.

How it fits the programme

Four points in a build where we are useful

STEP 01

After render and before landscaping

The messiest point. Getting splatter off the driveway and paths before the landscaper arrives saves cleaning the same surface twice.

STEP 02

Film and sticker removal

Well before handover, while the adhesive still releases cleanly. Left into summer this becomes a solvent job with a risk to the frames.

STEP 03

The handover clean

Three to five days before the date, so there is room to come back if a trade marks something afterwards.

STEP 04

Pre‑settlement defects

Where an inspection has raised an exterior item, usually glass or concrete, turned around quickly rather than scheduled.

Volume work

Estates, townhouses and multi lot sites

Priced per lot, not per visit

A rate per dwelling type lets you budget the exterior clean into the build cost rather than treating it as a variable at the end.

Sequenced with your programme

Lots cleaned as they come up to handover rather than all at once, so nothing is cleaned too early and dirtied again.

One contact, one invoice

Whether it is three townhouses or thirty lots across an estate, it is one scope and one account rather than a booking per house.

Rework on us if a trade marks it

Within a reasonable window before handover, if someone comes back and marks a surface we cleaned, we come back. It is a build site and that happens.

Questions

From builders and site managers

Do you do internal builders cleans as well?

No. We are exterior only and we quote that way deliberately. Most builders already have an internal cleaner, and splitting the scope cleanly means nothing is double paid for and nothing is assumed to be someone else's.

If you need the inside done we are happy to work alongside whoever does it and sequence around them.

How far ahead do you need to be booked?

For a single dwelling, a few days is usually enough. For an estate or a run of townhouses, the earlier we have the programme the better, because we schedule against your handover dates rather than against our diary.

Defect call backs are treated differently and we turn those around as fast as we can, because they are usually holding up a settlement.

What if a trade marks something after you have cleaned?

Within a reasonable window before handover, we come back and deal with it. It is a build site and it happens. What we will not do is clean a lot three weeks early because the programme says so and then treat the damage as a new job.

Timing the clean three to five days out is what avoids most of this.

Can you remove concrete slurry and render off a new driveway?

Yes, and it is better done soon. Fresh slurry and render run off come off a new slab without much difficulty. Left to cure through a summer, the same marks need acid at a controlled strength, and acid on new concrete has its own risk because the surface is still green.

Where it has gone that far it moves into mortar and cement residue removal and gets tested first.

Do you have insurance for working on site?

Insurance and induction requirements vary by builder and site, and we will provide whatever documentation your site requires before we attend. Tell us what you need at quote stage rather than at the gate.

Will you clean a house that has already been handed over?

Yes, though at that point it is usually a different job. Once the owner is in, the glazing has often already etched and the driveway has had cars on it. That becomes ordinary exterior cleaning with some restoration rather than a builders clean, and it is priced accordingly.
